summary: As weak as w14 and with more errors. Lines are mostly cookery and botany facts ('Is sprinkled into every soup and stew', 'Is ground into flour', 'Turns bubble tea purple'); about 80 Rares are facts rather than powers; about 95 Epics are crowd/harvest scenes ('was picked by every family', 'was sliced for every child at the picnic'); nearly all Legendaries are quiet successes, prize/show wins or 'stood for five hundred years' (tree, pine, cypress, fir, oak, olive tree, baobab). Several names are attached to the wrong lore: broccoli and cassava have Common/Uncommon names swapped; carrot, cucumber, tomato, pineapple, cranberry, maple tree, rosemary, papaya and horseradish have Legendary names describing a different line. Content flags: the twig Legendary points at a real author (high), the prune Epic mocks a care home with a toilet queue (high), star fruit Rare mentions cocktails and its Ultimate 'Star Burst' is a sweet brand, 'Pea Shooter' echoes a trademarked game plant, 'Purple Haze'-style issues are in w14. Cassava (must be cooked) now turns that into the joke. Cross-object copies: eggplant L = tofu L, dragon fruit L = lychee L, herbs L = thyme L, five 'stuck in your teeth' lines, melon R = papaya R, peach U = nectarine U, coconut L = coconut tree L, many '500 years' tree Legendaries. Mechanics: tree 'Leaf Blizzard' and fir 'Snow Drop' use cold words where a variant burns, herbs and oak Ultimates repeat the Epic name, beet 'Flash' and dragon fruit 'Crack' promise the wrong status, 'Grape Grape Grape' and 'Snap Snap' sound multi-hit on single hits. Replacement Legendary names deliberately mix shapes (only about 30 'X the Y'). Every high and medium item has a replacement; the patched batch validates and lints 0 high / 0 medium; names are unique across all curated content and the Pilot 01 proposal.
